2M.1 We are to give glory and praise unto God.

precepts.text: This people have I formed for myself; they shall shew forth my praise. Teach your children they are superior, because they are; the world shows them Superman and Batman and tells them they are criminals. Sons need fathers in the household who think like that.
precepts.point: I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations. Whatever the Lord ordained us to be, we will be, and he put talents in us. That is why the Bishop stresses organizing those talents; you cannot bring self-doubt around him. Get the doubt out and let the real you stay and be built up.

note.label: The Image of Dysfunction or the Image of God Which One Are You?

precepts.why:
“This people have I formed for myself; they shall shew forth my praise.” This people is the Israelites, Judah: God formed us for himself, to show forth his praise, and all the other nations will catch hell.

Put that in your spirit and put it in your children's spirit. Teach your children they are superior, because they are. The world tells us lies: it shows us Superman and Batman and all kinds of fools on TV and makes us think we are nothing but criminals. Then, when we say the reverse, they try the Jedi mind trick and make us think we are doing something wrong. That is why sons need fathers in the household who think this way, so they grow up in the right posture.

We were not formed for survival or to be a product of our environment. We were formed for a purpose that comes from outside our circumstances, connected to the nature and intent of the Most High who formed us. That is Jeremiah 1:5: “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee.” Before the sperm hit the egg, we already existed and were known by him, and he chose which spirit to send, this one rather than that one, for a purpose. “and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations”: whatever the Lord ordained us to be, we will be. He made us the children of Israel and put talents in us. That is why those talents must be organized and not wasted. Don't bring self-doubt; get the doubt out and let the real you stay and be built up.

precepts.text: So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous and destruction of the enemies. There can be no salvation of the oppressed without the destruction of the oppressor. That is so plain, but for Christians it's so difficult to understand.
precepts.point: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west; I will say to the north, give up; and to the south, keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.
precepts.why:
Isaiah says, “I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee”, and “therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.” When it says give men for thee, it means kill men for thee. We don’t have to do anything; God says, let me do it. Wisdom of Solomon shows why it must be that way: “So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.”

The salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies go together. There can be no salvation without the destruction of your enemies. There can be no salvation of the oppressed without the destruction of the oppressor. That is so plain, but for Christians it is so difficult to understand.

That is what happened in Egypt, and it is what Isaiah promises again. Egypt, Ethiopia and Seba were given for Israel’s ransom because Israel was “precious in my sight”, “honourable”, and loved of God. The nations fall in Israel’s place.

And with the destruction comes the gathering: “Fear not: for I am with thee: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west; I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.” The same judgment that destroys the oppressor sets the righteous free and brings every one that is called by his name home.

precepts.text: Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins nor receive of her plagues: God has told you who is conspiring and what to do, and his people are Israel.
precepts.point: Fear not, I will bring thy seed from the east and the west and say to the north, give up. Everyone called by my name I created for my glory; let the nations bring their witnesses, ye are my witnesses, and beside me there is no saviour. All the destruction is to set the twelve tribes back in their place.
precepts.why:
“I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee.” The Lord gave other nations for us: he brought blood and destruction on their heads on our behalf. “Since thou wast precious in my sight”, not yellow, black and white all precious in his sight like the Christian song says, but the twelve tribes, “therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.” He didn't say he would spare the little Arab kids or the Israeli kids planted in the land. Revelation shows how much he loves us in the middle of that.

He has put it in front of us in prophecy: what is about to go down, where it is going down, who is involved and who is conspiring against Israel, and the parts they will play. He has told us not to meddle with them, and he has told us what to do to secure our salvation.

“And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people.” Who are his people? According to Isaiah 3:12, children are their oppressors and women rule over them; only the southern kingdom and northern kingdom have that problem. So he is letting you know it is only Israel.

“That ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” Don't be part of the sins and the plagues coming on this place, the land of the north where Esau dwells, or in the valley of decision where everybody is gathering for the great day of Armageddon. Don't receive the death and destruction on the way when the Most High shows up.

So your fight is not with the nations. Your fight is with getting yourself together, working on your salvation, so you can see the promise made to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

precepts.text: Children are their oppressors and women rule over them: only Israel has that problem, so my people is Israel.
precepts.point: Fear not, I will bring thy seed from the east and the west and say to the north, give up. Everyone called by my name I created for my glory; let the nations bring their witnesses, ye are my witnesses, and beside me there is no saviour. All the destruction is to set the twelve tribes back in their place.
precepts.why:
Isaiah 43 says, “Since thou wast precious in my sight, thou hast been honourable, and I have loved thee: therefore will I give men for thee.” Who is the “thee” the Lord loves and gives other nations for? Revelation 18 says “Come out of her, my people”, and Isaiah 3 identifies who his people are.

“As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them.” There is only one people with that problem: the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom, Israel. We are the only ones living under it.

So “my people” is Israel, not all nations. The fools who want to engraft all the nations say, what about all nations? But if you acknowledge that we are the twelve tribes of Israel and still want to engraft every other nation in, when are you going to acknowledge that they have to give us back our land and everything that belongs to us? You won't. It's hypocrisy.

The Lord has not dealt with any other nation. “Even every one that is called by my name: for I have created him for my glory”, and “Ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord.” All the destruction coming on the other nations is to set the twelve tribes of Israel, those keeping the commandments and striving, back in their rightful place.

precepts.text: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west.
precepts.point: When the Lord shall roar like a lion, the children shall tremble from the west, the western hemisphere where the tribes are primarily scattered.
precepts.why:
Hosea says the Lord “shall roar like a lion: when he shall roar, then the children shall tremble from the west.” The west is the western hemisphere, where the tribes are primarily scattered.

Isaiah says the same: “Fear not: for I am with thee: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west”. The Lord gathers his children from where they are, and the west is where most of them are, here in America and this side of the world.

So when the Lord roars, the children who tremble and walk after him come from the west, and he gathers them. That is the hope for the tribes over here, but it comes with a warning. Before this the class read that Babylon's “sins have reached unto heaven”, and that we must come out of the ways of America and out of her idolatry. If we don't repent of our stubbornness, our bullheadedness and our idolatry, we will get the same judgment as her. The seed that is gathered from the west is the seed that answers the roar and walks after the Lord.

precepts.text: I will bring thy seed from the east and gather thee from the west; bring my sons from far and my daughters from the ends of the earth.
precepts.point: In Luke 20:16 they answered, God forbid: they would not give up their place.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Christ said many would come “from the east and west” and sit down with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Isaiah shows who they are.

“Fear not: for I am with thee: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west; I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth”. It is his seed, his sons and his daughters, brought back from the ends of the earth. That is going to us.

So the nation the kingdom is given to, the other husbandmen that render the Lord the fruits in their seasons, is not strangers. It is the seed of Jacob, gathered from the east, the west, the north and the south, the people “which not having heard of me yet shall believe me”, while the wicked elders, the children of the kingdom who rejected the stone, are cast out.

Whosoever falls on that stone shall be broken; but when Christ returns, on whomsoever it falls, it will grind him to powder.

precepts.text: To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, there is no light in them.
precepts.point: Let them bring forth their witnesses; ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord. Israel, the stick of Judah and the stick of Ephraim, are his witnesses.

note.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.why:
“Let all the nations be gathered together, and let the people be assembled: who among them can declare this, and shew us former things? let them bring forth their witnesses.” Who can show the things from the past? The next verse answers: “Ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord, and my servant whom I have chosen.” God’s witnesses on this earth are the children of Israel, and the two sticks, the stick of Judah and the stick of Ephraim, the southern and northern kingdoms, are two witnesses also.

What does a witness have? A testimony. A witness testifies, like a witness to a crime in a court of law. And we do not play a small role. Isaiah shows what God’s witnesses testify: “To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.”

As witnesses, what we are supposed to be testifying is the law and the testimony. If they do not speak according to this word, the law and the testimony, there is no light in them.

The testimony is what John bore record of: “the testimony of Jesus Christ, and of all things that he saw.” Part of that testimony is to identify “them which say they are Jews, and are not”, the synagogue of Satan. And Malachi’s testimony: “They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness.” The they who call them that are the witnesses, the prophets. So when the nations are gathered and asked for witnesses, Israel stands to the law and to the testimony.

precepts.text: Fill Zion with thine unspeakable oracles; give testimony unto those that thou hast possessed from the beginning.
precepts.point: Let them bring forth their witnesses; ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord. Israel, the stick of Judah and the stick of Ephraim, are his witnesses.

note.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.why:
“Ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord.” A witness has a testimony. What is the testimony Israel carries? Sirach shows where it came from: “Fill Sion with thine unspeakable oracles, and thy people with thy glory: Give testimony unto those that thou hast possessed from the beginning, and raise up prophets that have been in thy name.”

The testimonies are what God gave to Moses, to Jeremiah, to Nahum, to Micah, to Isaiah, to Peter, Paul and the apostles. All the things these men wrote are the testimony: testimonies of things that are going to happen in the future, of what is going to happen to the children of Israel.

So when the scripture says the witnesses have to testify, the testimony is what is written, what the prophets said is going to happen. That is why Isaiah 43:9 asks “who among them can declare this, and shew us former things?” No other nation can. Israel, the people God possessed from the beginning, was given the unspeakable oracles, and we testify them.

And as we testify, we bring forth judgment. Brought before governors and kings “for a testimony against them and the Gentiles”, it is not we who speak but the Spirit of our Father speaking in us. The wicked who hides as an angel of light is revealed and condemned, because the witnesses must testify first before God brings forth judgment, as in a court of law.

precepts.text: Bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.
precepts.point: The covetous Pharisees derided him. Ye are they which justify yourselves before men, but that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.

note.label: All Skinfolk Ain't Kinfolk: Children of Darkness

precepts.why:
“And the Pharisees also, who were covetous, heard all these things: and they derided him.” They were mad as hell at the Messiah. Christ answered, “Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts.” They are the ones going on podcasts arguing back and forth for fame, notoriety and publicity, wanting to be content creators, because “that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.” In the parable that follows, the Pharisees are the rich man, and Lazarus is the disciples, us, the people under their rulership.

Those who justify themselves before men are not the ones God gathers. Christ said “many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob”, and Isaiah shows who they are: “I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west; I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.”

Thy seed: the sons and daughters of Israel scattered to the ends of the earth. God tells the north to give them up and the south not to keep them back. Those are his children, brought in from far, while the covetous Pharisees who derided Christ, children of darkness who came back as the scribes and Sadducees, are cast out. All skinfolk ain't kinfolk.

precepts.text: We thy people, whom thou hast called thy firstborn, thy only begotten.
precepts.point: God will say to the north, give up, and to the south, keep not back, and bring his sons from far.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
“Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.” And to redeem us, “I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee. Since thou wast precious in my sight.” We are precious in his sight because we are the apple of his eye.

Ezra shows what we are to him: “But we thy people, whom thou hast called thy firstborn, thy only begotten, and thy fervent lover, are given into their hands.” We are his fervent lover. We are his bride. We are his wife.

That is why God gave Egypt, Ethiopia and Seba, which is Somalia, for our ransom: to deliver us out of captivity he had to destroy the Egyptian army, and Ethiopia that was a help to them. “therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.” In order for us to be delivered from slavery and captivity, God said, I have to destroy nations for them to release you.

So when Isaiah says “thou art mine”, it is the voice of a husband over his wife. The firstborn, the only begotten, the fervent lover given into the hands of the nations is the one God redeems.

precepts.text: Wherewith thou didst punish our adversaries, by the same thou didst glorify us.
precepts.point: God will say to the north, give up, and to the south, keep not back, and bring his sons from far.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
“I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.” Do you think the nations are just going to give his people back? No. Christ comes with armies: “And the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean.” Wherever the Israelites are, the armies of God will go there and deliver us and destroy those nations.

The Christian mentality wants a white Jesus to come back throwing flowers, and John Hagee says Christ will set his government up to get the Democrats and Republicans in order. Wisdom of Solomon shows what salvation really is: “So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” We all want the salvation of the righteous, and we have to accept the destruction of the enemy too. That is what we just read in Isaiah 43.

“For wherewith thou didst punish our adversaries, by the same thou didst glorify us, whom thou hadst called.” The same way he punishes our adversaries, he glorifies us. That is the bride of Christ: Christ is coming to get his woman. That is what the whole thing is about.

So the redeeming of Isaiah 43:1, “I have called thee by thy name”, is the calling of Wisdom 18: “us, whom thou hadst called”, glorified by the very judgment that punishes the nations holding us.

precepts.text: It shall no more be said, the Lord liveth that brought Israel out of Egypt.
precepts.point: God will say to the north, give up, and to the south, keep not back, and bring his sons from far.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
“I have redeemed thee.” Jeremiah shows that this redemption will be greater than the first: “Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that it shall no more be said, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.” When he delivered us out of Egypt, he destroyed Egypt, he destroyed Ethiopia and he destroyed Seba, Somalia.

“But, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north, and from all the lands whither he had driven them.” The land of the north is North America. All the lands whither he had driven them are the Caribbean, Africa, and all the different lands we are scattered in.

“and I will bring them again into their land that I gave unto their fathers.” That is Isaiah 43: “I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west.” We are here in the west, the western hemisphere.

So the redemption promised to Jacob is not the one out of ancient Egypt. It is the deliverance out of the land of the north and every land of our captivity, and it will be so great that the Exodus will no longer be what men speak of.

precepts.text: Creation shall be delivered into the glorious liberty of the children of God.
precepts.point: God will say to the north, give up, and to the south, keep not back, and bring his sons from far.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
“Fear not: for I have redeemed thee.” Paul shows what that redemption brings: “Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God.”

The creature itself is you and me. We shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. That is talking about us being delivered, not just from this body, but from captivity.

It is the same promise as Jeremiah 16: the Lord that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north and from all the lands whither he had driven them, bringing them again into the land he gave their fathers. Isaiah 43 says he will say to the north, Give up, and bring his sons and daughters from the ends of the earth.

So “I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine” ends in liberty: the children of God set free from bondage, the captives delivered in the year of jubilee.

precepts.text: I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee; since thou wast precious in my sight, I have loved thee, therefore will I give men for thee. A ransom secures the safe exit of the victim; the Most High gave Egypt and Ethiopia their own lives to bring Israel out.
precepts.point: I am the Lord your God, which brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan. The Most High is not the God of everybody: to bring Israel out He judged Egypt, and to give Israel Canaan He cast out the seven nations, greater and mightier than Israel, delivered them before Israel to be smitten, with no covenant and no mercy shewed, during that time period.

note.label: Leviticus 25: The Sabbath of the Land and the Year of Jubile

precepts.why:
“I am the Lord your God, which brought you forth out of the land of Egypt.” The Most High is not the God of everybody. To bring Israel out He judged Egypt: “I am the Lord thy God, the Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour: I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee.”

A ransom secures the safe exit of the victim. The Most High gave Egypt and Ethiopia their own lives to bring Israel out. “Since thou wast precious in my sight, thou hast been honourable, and I have loved thee: therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.” That is the God speaking in Leviticus 25:38.

precepts.text: For this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee; he raised Esau up just as he raised Pharaoh, to show his power and be destroyed for Israel's sake.
precepts.point: Fear not, for I am with thee; I will bring thy seed from the east and gather thee from the west, saying to the north give up and to the south keep not back, bringing my sons from far and my daughters from the ends of the earth. The Most High destroyed nations for us and will do it again.
precepts.why:
“I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee”, and “therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.” Paul shows how Egypt was given: “For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.”

For this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee. The Most High raised Pharaoh up to show his power in him and to be destroyed for Israel’s sake, and he raised Esau up just as he raised Pharaoh, to show his power and be destroyed for Israel’s sake. The Most High destroyed nations for us and will do it again, because “thou wast precious in my sight, thou hast been honourable, and I have loved thee”. So “Fear not: for I am with thee”: he will bring our seed from the east and gather us from the west, our sons from far and our daughters from the ends of the earth.

precepts.text: Yet now hear, O Jacob my servant, and Israel whom I have chosen; the servant and witness of the Lord is plainly named Israel.
precepts.point: I, even I, am the Lord, and beside me there is no saviour; I have declared and saved and shown when there was no strange god among you. Before the day was I am he, and there is none that can deliver out of my hand.
precepts.why:
“Ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord, and my servant whom I have chosen”. Who is that servant and witness? Read straight on into the next chapter: “Yet now hear, O Jacob my servant; and Israel, whom I have chosen”. The servant and witness of the Lord is plainly named Israel.

This kills the Jehovah’s Witness doctrine, because Jacob is the subject, so the witnesses are Israel. Israel, the blind people that have eyes and the deaf that have ears, is brought forth before all the nations gathered together, and Israel is the witness “that ye may know and believe me, and understand that I am he: before me there was no God formed, neither shall there be after me.” “I, even I, am the Lord; and beside me there is no saviour.”

precepts.text: He showed his word, statutes, and judgments unto Jacob and Israel; he has not dealt so with any nation, for no other nation knows the judgments of God.
precepts.point: Therefore I have profaned the princes of the sanctuary and given Jacob to the curse and Israel to reproaches. The Most High gave Jacob to the curse.
precepts.why:
“Therefore I have profaned the princes of the sanctuary, and have given Jacob to the curse, and Israel to reproaches.” Why Jacob? “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel. He hath not dealt so with any nation: and as for his judgments, they have not known them. Praise ye the Lord.”

The Most High showed his word, his statutes and his judgments unto Jacob and Israel; he has not dealt so with any nation, for no other nation knows the judgments of God. Because Israel alone was given the word, Israel alone is held to it: “thou hast made me to serve with thy sins, thou hast wearied me with thine iniquities”, “Thy first father hath sinned, and thy teachers have transgressed against me”, and so the Most High gave Jacob to the curse.

precepts.text: Whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth; they that are without the chastisement that all are partakers of are bastards and not sons, and Israel alone knows this chastisement.
precepts.point: Therefore I have profaned the princes of the sanctuary and given Jacob to the curse and Israel to reproaches. The Most High gave Jacob to the curse.
precepts.why:
The Most High gave Jacob to the curse, and that curse is chastisement: “For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.”

Whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth. They that are without the chastisement that all are partakers of are bastards and not sons, and Israel alone knows this chastisement. So Jacob given to the curse and Israel to reproaches is the Father dealing with sons: he is the same one “that blotteth out thy transgressions for mine own sake, and will not remember thy sins”, who says, “Put me in remembrance: let us plead together”.

precepts.text: The opening of the curses for breaking the laws, running from verse fifteen through sixty-eight, the punishments that came upon Israel.
precepts.point: Therefore I have profaned the princes of the sanctuary and given Jacob to the curse and Israel to reproaches. The Most High gave Jacob to the curse.
precepts.why:
“Therefore I have profaned the princes of the sanctuary, and have given Jacob to the curse”. The curse is written: “But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”.

This is the opening of the curses for breaking the laws, running from verse fifteen through sixty-eight, the punishments that came upon Israel. Israel did not hearken, did not bring the small cattle of the burnt offerings, made him to serve with their sins and wearied him with their iniquities, and thy first father hath sinned and thy teachers have transgressed, so all these curses came upon Jacob and overtook him. That is the curse the Most High gave Jacob to, and the reproaches he gave Israel to.

precepts.text: Thus saith the Lord that created thee O Jacob and formed thee O Israel, fear not, for I have redeemed thee and called thee by thy name, thou art mine.
precepts.point: Both young men and old shall rejoice in the dance, for He will turn their mourning into joy, comfort them, and satiate the soul of the priest with fatness, and His people shall be satisfied with His goodness.
precepts.why:
“For the Lord hath redeemed Jacob, and ransomed him from the hand of him that was stronger than he.” Isaiah says who did the redeeming and who was redeemed: “But now thus saith the Lord that created thee, O Jacob, and he that formed thee, O Israel, Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.”

He that created Jacob and formed Israel is the one that redeemed him. He called Israel by name, and Israel is his. So the nations are to hear and declare it in the isles afar off: he that scattered Israel will gather him and keep him as a shepherd does his flock, and they shall come and sing in the height of Zion and sorrow no more, because they belong to him.

precepts.text: Israel is the people the Most High formed for Himself to show forth His praise, which is fulfilled as they return to His law before the nations.
precepts.point: He gathers them out of their enemies' land, as we are being gathered today from the four corners of the earth, and He is sanctified in them in the sight of many nations. The heathen had nothing to do with our captivity; it was the Lord's will, and no one can resist the will of the Lord. He leaves none of them among the heathen anymore, and He will not hide His face anymore, for He has poured out His spirit upon the house of Israel.

note.label: Ezekiel 39: The Fall of Gog and the Gathering of Israel

precepts.why:
“This people have I formed for myself; they shall shew forth my praise.” Israel is the people the Most High formed for Himself, and that is why He brings again the captivity of Jacob and has mercy upon the whole house of Israel, upon those who repent and endure to the end. He is jealous for His holy name.

He gathers them out of their enemies' lands, as we are being gathered today from the four corners of the earth, and is “sanctified in them in the sight of many nations”. As they return to His law before the nations, they show forth His praise. Then they know that He is the Lord their God, “which caused them to be led into captivity among the heathen”. The heathen had nothing to do with our captivity; it was the Lord's will, and no one can resist the will of the Lord.

He has gathered them to their own land and “left none of them any more there”. He will not hide His face any more, for He has poured out His spirit upon the house of Israel: the people formed for Himself, showing forth His praise.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 11 A Time Of Defamation

precepts.why: Who are the two witnesses? This is the same scripture Jehovah's Witnesses like to use to justify calling themselves Jehovah's Witnesses, but verse 1 tells you who the witnesses are. “But now thus saith the Lord that created thee, O Jacob, and he that formed thee, O Israel, Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.” So it is talking about the Israelites. Then verse 10: ye are my witnesses.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 11 A Time Of Defamation

precepts.why: “Ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord, and my servant whom I have chosen: that ye may know and believe me, and understand that I am he: before me there was no God formed, neither shall there be after me.” Ye are my witnesses: so the witnesses are the Israelites. The witnesses are not all nations that believe in Jesus; understand that thing. The witnesses are Israel, making reference to the two kingdoms.

God is saying, the same way I destroyed ancient Egypt, Ethiopia, and the Sabeans, I must destroy nations again for your deliverance. Fear not: for I am with thee: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west; I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back. Bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth, even every one that is called by my name. That is why we have to teach our people: you are the Israelites the Bible speaks of.

When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned. All of this we are learning is for us to have faith, brothers and sisters, for when the time comes: all this rich history of God fighting for us as a people is for us to have faith and hope.

All the destruction is to set the twelve tribes back in their place.

Thus saith the Lord that created thee, O Jacob, fear not. When you see war all over the world, the prophecy has to come to pass; the Bishop taught a whole series on Revelation years ago to prepare you.

points: But now thus saith the Lord that created thee O Jacob and formed thee O Israel: fear not, for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name, thou art mine. When thou passest through the waters I will be with thee, and through the fire thou shalt not be burned.

For I am the Lord thy God, the Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour; I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee. Since thou wast precious in my sight and honorable, and I have loved thee, I will give men for thee and people for thy life.

Fear not, for I am with thee; I will bring thy seed from the east and gather thee from the west, saying to the north give up and to the south keep not back, bringing my sons from far and my daughters from the ends of the earth. The Most High destroyed nations for us and will do it again.

Bring forth the blind people that have eyes and the deaf that have ears; let all the nations be gathered and assembled. Who among them can declare this and show us former things? Let them bring their witnesses that they may be justified.

Ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord, and my servant whom I have chosen, that ye may know and believe and understand that I am he; before me there was no God formed, neither shall there be after me. This kills the Jehovah's Witness doctrine, because Jacob is the subject, so the witnesses are Israel.

I, even I, am the Lord, and beside me there is no saviour; I have declared and saved and shown when there was no strange god among you. Before the day was I am he, and there is none that can deliver out of my hand.

Thus saith the Lord your redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: for your sake I have sent to Babylon and brought down all the nobles and the Chaldeans whose cry is in the ships. I am the Lord your Holy One, the creator of Israel, your King.

Thus saith the Lord which maketh a way in the sea and a path in the mighty waters, which bringeth forth the chariot and horse, the army and the power; they shall lie down together and not rise, extinct and quenched as tow.

Remember ye not the former things; behold I will do a new thing, making a way in the wilderness and rivers in the desert. He remembers how he made water come out of the rock and fed us manna and quail in the wilderness where no man dwelt, supplying our every need.
The beasts of the field shall honour me because I give water in the wilderness for my people, my chosen; this people have I formed for myself, they shall show forth my praise.

But thou hast not called upon me, O Jacob, and thou hast been weary of me, O Israel; thou hast not brought the small cattle of thy burnt offerings nor honoured me with thy sacrifices, but made me to serve with thy sins and wearied me with thine iniquities.

I, even I, am he that blotteth out thy transgressions for mine own sake, and will not remember thy sins; put me in remembrance, let us plead together. Thy first father hath sinned and thy teachers have transgressed against me.
Therefore I have profaned the princes of the sanctuary and given Jacob to the curse and Israel to reproaches. The Most High gave Jacob to the curse.
